claim: [MOZILLA ADVOCACY DATA — interested party] Mozilla claims Firefox has been selected via a DMA choice screen every 10 seconds, totaling over 6 million selections, with 5x higher retention for choice-screen selectors versus an unspecified baseline.
stance_target: ecosystem lock-in is purely structural preference, not regulation-removable inertia
scope_conditions: EU iOS/Android browser choice screens, measurement window unspecified (roughly Mar 2024-May 2026); source is an interested party benefiting from this narrative — treat as advocacy data pending independent corroboration
quoted_support: Firefox is selected through a DMA browser choice screen every 10 seconds. That adds up to more than six million Firefox selections. And people are sticking with us: retention is five times higher when people choose Firefox through a choice screen.

claim: An NBER working paper (w35112) using a difference-in-differences design comparing EU vs. 43 non-EU countries found Firefox daily active users were 113% higher than the counterfactual on iOS and 12% higher on Android in the 15 months following DMA choice-screen rollout, with the effect reportedly growing over time.
stance_target: switching under DMA choice screens is small or non-persistent (i.e. lock-in is structural preference)
scope_conditions: EU vs 43 non-EU countries, 15 months pre/post iOS and Android choice screen rollout
quoted_support: Independent researchers compared Firefox daily active users in the EU with 43 non-EU countries... they found that Firefox daily active users (DAU) were 113% higher in the EU than it would have been without the DMA. On Android, it was 12% higher.

claim: Even Mozilla concedes choice screens are 'not a silver bullet' and that ecosystem lock-in and interoperability barriers continue to constrain competition despite browser choice-screen gains, and that desktop (roughly 310 million EU devices) remains entirely untouched by choice-screen mandates.
stance_target: lock-in is structural/durable rather than fully regulation-removable, at least outside narrow mandated-choice contexts
scope_conditions: EU desktop and mobile browser markets
quoted_support: desktop remains largely untouched – leaving roughly 310 million desktops and laptops in the EU without equivalent browser choice... ecosystem lock-in and interoperability barriers still hold back competition and innovation.
numbers: 310 million EU desktops/laptops without choice-screen coverage
